threads.thread_goal: Align on target segments and final MVP bundle list.

messages.text:
Kicking off the segment and MVP bundle alignment for the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles.
I have uploaded a first pass of target segments and bundle ideas into the catalog draft in A1, and logged the related work under T1 and T2 in the integrated plan A6.
Proposal for target segments:
- Mid-market multi-site businesses
- Enterprise accounts with existing contracts up for renewal in the next 9 months
- High-growth digital natives with distributed teams
For each, I mapped a small set of bundles (Connectivity Core, Connectivity Plus, Managed Workplace, and Support Priority) with high-level features and indicative SLAs.
Before we go deeper, can you review whether these segments match what you see in the field and from a delivery standpoint?
If we can converge here, we can then freeze the MVP bundle list and park the rest in the backlog.

Thanks for starting this.
From the project plan side in A6, I see T1 marked as in progress but not yet baselined.
Quick questions so I can update the RAID section:
- For mid-market multi-site, are we assuming existing support channels, or do we need a different SLA tier from what is in A1 now?
- For digital natives, do we expect more self-service and fewer on-site interventions?
I want to be sure we do not overload operations when we lock the MVP bundles.

Looking at A1 now.
On the delivery side, I am slightly concerned about the Support Priority bundle for enterprise renewals.
Right now, our standard SLA in the checklist I keep for ops is 8x5 for most B2B.
In A1, I see 24x7 response for some of the proposed bundles.
Do we already have confirmation from support management that they can staff that, or should we mark that as an assumption in T2 and T6?

Good questions.
For mid-market multi-site, the intent is to keep them on the current support channels and SLAs, so no new tier there.
For digital natives, yes, the idea is more self-service and remote support, which is why in A1 you will see a stronger focus on portal access and proactive notifications rather than on-site visits.
I will add these as explicit assumptions in T2 and flag them in A6 so they are visible in the RAID log.
On the 24x7 point from M3, I will answer in that reply so we keep the thread clear.

On the 24x7 SLA for Support Priority: this is currently a proposal, not a confirmed commitment.
I have not yet secured a formal sign-off from support management.
My suggestion is:
- Keep 24x7 in the MVP definition in A1 as a differentiator for top enterprise renewals.
- Log a dependency in A6 under T2 and T6 that operations must confirm staffing before launch.
If that feels too risky, we can downgrade to extended hours (for example 12x5) for the first wave.
What is your view from the project side, @82217 and @83919?

From a risk perspective, I would rather not promise 24x7 until we have a written confirmation from support.
Could we define the MVP bundle as extended hours now and add 24x7 as a roadmap enhancement in a later wave?
That way, in T1 and T2 we still keep the structure, but in A1 we mark 24x7 as future.
I can add a risk entry in A6 so we track the potential upgrade.

I agree with keeping it conservative for the first launch.
If we go with extended hours for Support Priority in the MVP, operations can probably handle that with current staffing.
We can still prepare the process for 24x7 in parallel, but not commit it in A1 yet.
So I support the idea of marking 24x7 as post-launch in the roadmap section of the catalog.

I went through the segment list and the bundle names in A1.
From a marketing and channel perspective, the three segments you listed make sense and are easy to brief to sales.
One question: do we want a separate bundle for small professional offices, or do we keep them under mid-market multi-site for now?
If we add too many variants, it might complicate T1 and T2 and confuse the field.

I share the concern about too many variants.
Given the fixed launch date and the constraints in the project plan A6, I would keep small professional offices inside the mid-market multi-site segment for the first wave.
We can still capture their specific needs in the notes of A1 and revisit after launch.
Otherwise T1 will keep expanding and we risk scope creep.

Agree with both of you.
For the first launch, I suggest we do not create a separate bundle for small professional offices.
We will treat them as a sub-profile within mid-market multi-site and document any specific needs in A1.
I will also add a note in T1 that a dedicated bundle for that segment is a candidate for a later wave.

To keep the schedule under control, I propose we explicitly list the MVP bundles now so I can baseline them in A6 under T6.
From what I see in A1 and the discussion so far, the candidates are:
- Connectivity Core
- Connectivity Plus
- Managed Workplace
- Support Priority (with extended hours, not 24x7, for the first wave)
Can we confirm that these four are the only bundles for the MVP, and that any other ideas go into a post-launch backlog?

From my side, those four bundles are enough to build clear messaging and avoid confusion in the field.
We can always add more later once we see adoption and feedback.
So I am fine with freezing the MVP list at those four and parking the rest in a roadmap section in A1.

No objections from me.
From a delivery and readiness perspective, these four bundles are manageable within the current ERP and billing constraints we have noted in A6.
Anything more would probably require extra configuration work that we have not planned in T6 yet.
So I support freezing the MVP bundle list at these four.

Same here, I am aligned with the four-bundle MVP.
I will make sure the catalog structure in A1 is clean and that any additional bundle ideas are clearly marked as post-launch.
That should help avoid confusion when we brief sales later.

Great, we have convergence on the MVP bundle list.
I will update A1 so that:
- The four MVP bundles are clearly tagged as Wave 1.
- 24x7 support is moved to a roadmap note, not part of the initial SLA.
- Additional bundle ideas are listed in a separate section as future waves.
This will also close the scope part of T1 and T2 for the MVP.

Before we close this thread, we still need to formally approve the target segments for the first launch so I can lock them in A6 and communicate to stakeholders.
To recap, the proposal is:
- Mid-market multi-site businesses (including small professional offices as a sub-profile)
- Enterprise accounts with contracts up for renewal in the next 9 months
- High-growth digital natives with distributed teams
Can everyone confirm that these are the only target segments for Wave 1?

Confirmed from my side.
These three segments are clear enough for marketing and sales planning, and they match the constraints we discussed.
I will use exactly these in the early GTM drafts.

Also confirmed.
No additional segments from operations that we can realistically support for the first wave.
I will reflect these three in the readiness view I keep linked to A6.

Aligned as well.
I will make sure the segment tags in A1 match exactly these three so we avoid any ambiguity later.

Thanks all.
I am recording that we have:
- Approved the three target segments for Wave 1.
- Frozen the MVP bundle list at four bundles, with 24x7 support moved to a later wave.
I will update A1, close the scope part of T1 and T2 for the MVP, and confirm to sales and marketing in the next channel update.

threads.thread_goal: Converge on pricing, discounts, and margin guardrails.

messages.text:
Starting the pricing and margin discussion for the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles.
I have uploaded the first draft of the pricing and margin model in A2, based on the MVP bundles defined in A1.
The model covers list prices, standard discounts by segment, and a preliminary margin view, aligned with T3 and the KPI thinking in T10.
Key points:
- Target margin range currently sits between 32 percent and 38 percent across bundles.
- Standard discount bands by segment: up to 10 percent for mid-market, 15 percent for enterprise renewals, 8 percent for digital natives.
Please review A2 and share any concerns on the ranges or discount rules before we take this to finance for formal approval.

I went through A2.
From a market and channel perspective, the list prices look broadly in line with what we see from competitors, but the discount band for enterprise renewals might be a bit tight.
In practice, sales often needs up to 20 percent to win back accounts at risk.
Could we define a standard band up to 15 percent, with a controlled exception process up to 20 percent for specific cases, so we do not break the margin guardrails in T3?

Looking at A2 now.
I see the margin range you mentioned, but I am not fully sure how the discount rules interact with the KPIs in T10.
If we allow higher discounts for enterprise renewals, do we still stay above the minimum margin target in the project constraints?
Do we need a separate guardrail for each bundle, or can we define a single minimum margin across all bundles?

Good point.
From what I see in A2, the sensitivity tab shows that if we go to 20 percent discount on enterprise renewals, some bundles drop close to 30 percent margin.
Given the project constraint to maintain or improve current gross margin, I would suggest we set a hard minimum margin per bundle, not just overall.
Maybe we can agree that no deal should go below 30 percent margin without finance approval.

On the enterprise renewals discount band: I like the idea of a standard band plus an exception process.
In A2, I can set:
- Standard discount up to 15 percent for enterprise renewals.
- Exception band up to 20 percent, but only if the resulting margin stays above a defined minimum.
We can then document the approval flow with finance in T3.
I will also add a note in T10 so that we track the impact of these exceptions on revenue and margin KPIs.

On the margin guardrails: my proposal is to define a target range and a hard floor.
Based on A2, I suggest:
- Target margin range: 32 percent to 38 percent for most deals.
- Hard minimum margin per bundle: 30 percent, below which finance must approve.
This way, we respect the project constraint on gross margin while giving sales some flexibility.
If we agree, I will reflect this in A2 and in the documentation for T3.

I am not as deep into pricing, but I checked the summary tab in A2.
From a delivery cost perspective, the assumptions look reasonable, but I want to flag that if suppliers push back on their rates later, the margin could shrink.
Maybe we should add a note in T3 that supplier cost changes are a risk to the margin, and link it to the supplier work in T4.

The target range of 32 to 38 percent and a hard floor at 30 percent works for me.
It gives us enough room to compete while keeping a clear rule for exceptions.
For communication to sales, we should keep the message simple: standard discounts by segment and a clear minimum margin they cannot cross without approval.

I am comfortable with that structure.
For the project documentation in A6, I will record:
- Target margin range: 32 to 38 percent.
- Minimum margin per bundle: 30 percent, with finance approval required below that.
This will also help when we do the go/no-go review later.
So I support locking these as our guardrails.

Aligned with the proposed guardrails.
I will double-check the formulas in A2 to ensure the margin floor is correctly calculated for each bundle and segment.
If I spot any anomalies, I will comment directly in the sheet.

Thanks for the feedback.
I will now update A2 to reflect:
- Target margin range 32 to 38 percent.
- Hard minimum margin per bundle at 30 percent.
- Standard and exception discount bands by segment, with finance approval required below the margin floor.
This will complete the core of T3 before we take it to finance for sign-off.

Next step is to agree on the initial price list that will go into the sales materials and one-pagers.
Based on A2, I propose we:
- Use the list prices in the 'MVP bundles' tab as the official starting point.
- Include only the standard discount bands in the sales documentation, and keep the exception rules in an internal note.
If we all agree, I will mark this as the initial price list for inclusion in the sales enablement work and log it in A6.

I am fine using the MVP bundles tab in A2 as the source of truth for the initial price list.
For the sales one-pagers and GTM content, we will show list prices and typical discount ranges by segment, but not the exception rules.
That should keep the message simple while staying aligned with the guardrails.

Agreed.
I will reference the same tab in A2 when drafting the pricing section of the sales one-pagers later under T8, so we avoid any mismatch.
If we change anything after finance review, we will update A2 and the materials together.

No objections from my side.
Using a single tab in A2 as the reference will also make it easier to check consistency during the readiness review.
So I support signing off this initial price list for inclusion in sales materials.

Summarizing this thread:
- We agreed on a target margin range of 32 to 38 percent and a hard minimum margin per bundle of 30 percent, with finance approval required below that.
- We defined standard and exception discount bands by segment, with enterprise renewals allowed up to 15 percent standard and 20 percent with approval.
- We agreed to use the MVP bundles tab in A2 as the initial price list for sales materials.
I will finalize A2 accordingly, complete T3 for the pricing model, and share the file with finance for formal sign-off.

threads.thread_goal: Lock supplier engagement steps and system readiness scope.

messages.text:
Starting the supplier and systems readiness alignment for the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles.
I have updated the integrated project plan and RAID log in A6, and added a first draft of the supplier engagement view in A5, linked to T4 and T7.
Highlights:
- Key suppliers mapped to each MVP bundle, with proposed SLA changes.
- Initial list of contracts that might need updates.
- Draft scope for ERP and billing changes under T7.
Please review A5 and the relevant sections in A6 so we can confirm which supplier contracts must be updated before launch and what we consider as go or no-go criteria for ERP and billing.

I checked A5.
For Connectivity Core and Connectivity Plus, the main network supplier is already on 8x5 SLAs, but we are proposing extended hours in the MVP.
That means we definitely need to update that contract.
For Managed Workplace, the hardware supplier terms seem fine as is.
So at minimum, I would say the network supplier contract is a must-update before launch.
Do we also need to touch the backup connectivity supplier, or can that wait?

Good catch.
For the MVP bundles, the primary network supplier must align to the extended hours SLA, so that contract update is mandatory.
The backup connectivity supplier is used only in a subset of enterprise deals and mostly as a resilience option.
Given the timeline, I would suggest we keep the backup supplier as is for Wave 1 and treat any SLA upgrade there as a post-launch improvement.
I will mark the primary network supplier contract as must-update in A5 and A6.

Looking at A5, I also see a proposed change for the remote support outsourcing partner to cover extended hours.
Do we have any indication from them that they can take this on within the current budget, or is that still an open negotiation?
If it is not confirmed, we should flag it as a dependency in A6 under T4.

We had an initial conversation with the remote support partner, but nothing formal yet.
You are right, this is still an open negotiation.
I will log it as a dependency in A6 under T4 and mark the contract as 'target for update' in A5.
If they cannot meet the SLA within budget, we may need a fallback plan, maybe by adjusting the SLA or using internal teams.

From a customer promise perspective, the key is that whatever we put in A1 and in the GTM materials is fully backed by supplier SLAs.
So I would say any supplier that underpins the extended hours support or the managed services in the MVP bundles must have updated contracts before launch.
Optional add-ons or roadmap features can wait.
Maybe we can list those critical suppliers explicitly in A5 as 'must-update before launch'.

Agree.
Based on A5 and the MVP bundle definitions in A1, I propose the following list of supplier contracts that must be updated before launch:
- Primary network supplier (to align to extended hours SLA for Connectivity Core and Plus).
- Remote support outsourcing partner (to cover extended hours for Support Priority, subject to budget).
- Cloud service provider for Managed Workplace monitoring (to confirm data retention and reporting terms).
All other suppliers can be handled post-launch.
If we align on this, we can record it as our confirmed list.

This list makes sense to me.
These three suppliers are directly tied to the SLAs we are promising in the MVP bundles.
I would just add a note in A5 that if the remote support partner cannot meet the terms, we will adjust the SLA in A1 rather than delay the launch.

Aligned with the three must-update contracts.
I will help by checking the current clauses for the cloud service provider so we know exactly what needs to change.
We should also make sure the timing of these negotiations is reflected in A6 so it does not slip past the launch date.

I will record these three as 'must-update before launch' in A5 and A6.
Any other supplier changes will be tagged as post-launch.
This gives us a clear focus for T4 and helps manage the schedule.
Now we should align on the ERP and billing readiness criteria under T7.

On ERP and billing readiness, the draft in A6 under T7 lists several items.
To keep it practical, I suggest we define go or no-go criteria as:
- All four MVP bundles configured in ERP with correct product codes and tax rules.
- Billing system able to handle recurring charges and discounts as defined in A2.
- At least one test order per bundle successfully processed end to end.
Anything beyond that can be part of continuous improvement.

I like that structure.
From a product and pricing perspective, I would add one more criterion:
- Discount rules in the billing system must match the standard bands defined in A2, so we do not accidentally allow deeper discounts without approval.
If we include that, I am comfortable using these as our ERP and billing readiness criteria.

From a customer and sales experience angle, I would also like to ensure that the bundle names and descriptions in ERP match what we use in A1 and in the sales materials.
Otherwise, sales will get confused when they search for the bundles in the system.
Could we add that as part of the readiness criteria as well?

Putting this together, the proposed ERP and billing readiness criteria are:
- All four MVP bundles configured in ERP with correct product codes, tax rules, and names matching A1.
- Billing system able to handle recurring charges and standard discounts as defined in A2.
- At least one test order per bundle processed end to end, including invoicing.
- Discount rules in billing aligned with the standard bands, with no way to exceed them without approval.
If everyone agrees, I will record these criteria in A6 under T7 as our go or no-go definition.

These criteria look complete to me.
They cover configuration, pricing, and a basic operational test.
I support using them as the go or no-go definition for ERP and billing readiness.

Agreed.
I will coordinate with the ERP and billing teams to plan the test orders and confirm when we meet these criteria.
We will update A6 with the test results as we go.

Aligned as well.
I will double-check that the bundle names and discount rules in A1 and A2 are consistent so the ERP configuration team has a clean reference.
Once that is done, we can proceed with the configuration under T7.

To summarize this thread:
- We confirmed three supplier contracts that must be updated before launch: primary network supplier, remote support outsourcing partner, and cloud service provider for monitoring.
- All other supplier changes are moved to post-launch.
- We agreed on ERP and billing readiness criteria covering configuration of the four MVP bundles, correct pricing and discount rules, matching names, and successful test orders.
I will update A5 and A6 accordingly and continue driving T4 and T7 with the relevant teams.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize go-to-market plan and sales enablement materials.

messages.text:
Starting the GTM and sales enablement alignment for the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles.
I have shared a draft GTM playbook in A3 and initial sales one-pagers in A7, based on the MVP bundles in A1 and the pricing in A2.
This work ties into T5 and T8, and I have noted the internal communication dependencies for T11.
Key elements in A3:
- Positioning and key messages per target segment.
- Channel tactics for direct sales and partners.
- High-level launch campaign outline.
Please review A3 and A7 and share feedback on messaging, structure, and any gaps before we lock the plan and materials.

I reviewed A3 and A7.
Overall, the positioning aligns well with the bundle definitions in A1 and the pricing tiers in A2.
One suggestion: for the enterprise renewals segment, we should emphasize the improved SLAs and simplified bundle structure as the main value drivers.
Also, in the Connectivity Plus one-pager in A7, we should clarify that extended hours support is included, but 24x7 is not part of the first wave.
I can help refine the product descriptions if needed.

I also went through A7.
The structure of the one-pagers is clear: benefits, key features, and FAQs.
For the digital natives segment, maybe we can highlight the self-service portal and proactive monitoring more strongly, since that is a differentiator.
In A3, we might want to add a short section on how to handle pricing objections using the margin guardrails from A2.

From the project side, I am mainly checking consistency.
In A3, the launch timeline references some milestones that need to match A6.
I noticed the partner enablement webinar is scheduled a week earlier in A3 than in the project plan.
We should align those dates so we do not confuse stakeholders.
Also, for T11, we need to be clear which internal audiences get which messages and when.

I am looking at the FAQs in A7.
There are a few operational questions that might need more precise answers, such as response times and escalation paths.
We should make sure these match the SLAs we agreed in A1 and the supplier commitments in A5.
Otherwise, support teams might get unexpected requests.

Thanks for the detailed feedback.
I will:
- Update the enterprise renewals messaging in A3 to highlight improved SLAs and simplified bundles.
- Adjust the Connectivity Plus one-pager in A7 to clearly state extended hours support only, with 24x7 as a future enhancement.
- Strengthen the digital natives messaging around self-service and proactive monitoring as suggested in M57.
Once updated, I will share a new version for a quick final check.

On the timeline alignment: good catch.
I will adjust the partner enablement webinar date in A3 to match the milestone in A6.
For T11, I have a draft internal audience map in the appendix of A3, but I can make it more explicit:
- Sales and account managers.
- Customer support and operations.
- Partner managers.
Each with tailored key messages and timing.
I will refine that section and call it out clearly.

On the operational FAQs, I can help tighten the wording.
We should base the response times and escalation paths on the final SLA matrix in A1 and the supplier plan in A5.
I will propose updated answers for those questions and share them with you and support management for a quick validation before we freeze A7.

One more suggestion for A3: it might help to include a simple talk track for handling discount discussions, referencing the standard bands and margin floor from A2.
This will keep sales aligned with the pricing rules we agreed in T3.
I can draft a short section and send it to you for inclusion.

From a readiness perspective, I would like to confirm that once we approve A3 and A7, we treat them as the baseline for launch.
Any later changes should go through a simple change control so we do not end up with multiple versions in the field.
I will reference the final versions in A6 under the communication and enablement milestones.

I have now applied the updates discussed:
- Messaging tweaks for enterprise renewals and digital natives in A3.
- Clarified SLAs and removed any reference to 24x7 from the MVP one-pagers in A7.
- Aligned the partner webinar date with A6 and clarified internal audiences for T11.
Unless there are strong objections, I propose we approve A3 as the GTM plan for Wave 1, including the key launch campaigns outlined there.

From my side, A3 now reflects the product and pricing decisions accurately.
The segment-specific messages and the campaign outline look solid.
I support approving A3 as the GTM plan for the first launch, with the understanding that any major changes go through a quick review with us and marketing leadership.

I am aligned as well.
The GTM plan in A3 is clear and actionable, and the campaign elements are realistic for the timeline we have.
I support treating this as the baseline GTM plan for Wave 1.

No objections from operations.
The commitments in A3 and A7 match what we have planned with suppliers and systems.
I am comfortable approving A3 as the GTM plan.

Great, thanks for the confirmations.
Next, we should formally confirm the final versions of the sales one-pagers in A7 for distribution.
I have checked that pricing, SLAs, and bundle names match A1, A2, and the supplier plan in A5.
Unless anyone spots an issue, I propose we mark the current A7 set as final for sales enablement and upload them to the shared repository referenced in T8.

I did a final pass on A7.
Everything is consistent with A1 and A2, and the FAQs now reflect the agreed SLAs and escalation paths.
I support marking these one-pagers as final and sharing them with sales and partners.

From the project plan perspective, I will reference the final A7 set in A6 under the sales enablement milestone.
This will also be part of the readiness checklist later.
I am fine with treating the current A7 as final for distribution.

Aligned.
I will help ensure the final A7 files are correctly stored in the shared repository and that links are added to the channel so sales can find them easily.

To wrap up this thread:
- We approved A3 as the GTM plan for Wave 1, including key launch campaigns and internal communication mapping.
- We confirmed the final versions of the sales one-pagers in A7 for distribution, aligned with A1, A2, and A5.
I will now finalize T5 and T8, coordinate with HR and internal comms for T11, and share the final links in the channel.

threads.thread_goal: Run launch readiness check and define post-launch follow-up.

messages.text:
We are one week away from the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles, so starting the readiness and follow-up thread.
I have shared the latest Launch Readiness Checklist in A4, updated the project plan and RAID log in A6, and drafted the post-launch KPI framework in A8, linked to T9, T10, and T12.
In A4, each functional lead has a section to confirm status and any open gaps.
Please review your areas and update A4, then use this thread to call out any blockers or risks before we make the final go or no-go call.

I have updated the product and pricing sections in A4.
Status from my side:
- Bundle definitions and SLAs in A1 are final and reflected in A7.
- Pricing and discount rules in A2 are approved and shared with finance.
- No open issues on product scope for the MVP.
The only minor risk is potential supplier delays on the remote support partner, but we have a fallback SLA adjustment plan documented in A5.
From a product and pricing standpoint, I am comfortable proceeding.

I have filled in the operations and systems sections in A4.
Summary:
- ERP and billing configuration for the four MVP bundles is complete, and we have run at least one test order per bundle.
- Discount rules in billing match the standard bands from A2.
- A couple of minor issues on invoice layout are still being fixed, but they do not block launch.
I have logged these as issues in A6 with owners and due dates before launch.

Marketing and sales enablement status in A4:
- GTM plan in A3 is approved and all launch activities are scheduled.
- Sales one-pagers in A7 are final and shared with sales and partners.
- Internal communication messages for T11 are drafted and aligned with HR and internal comms.
No major gaps from my side.
We will monitor early adoption closely using the KPIs defined in A8.

I reviewed the checklist in A4 and the RAID log in A6.
The main open items I see are:
- Final confirmation from the remote support partner on extended hours coverage.
- Completion of the last invoice layout fixes mentioned in M76.
Both are tracked with owners and due dates before launch.
I do not see any critical risk that would justify delaying the launch, as long as we keep the fallback SLA adjustment ready in A5.

Thanks for the updates.
From the consolidated view in A4 and A6:
- All critical path items are either complete or on track for completion before launch.
- No high-severity risks remain without a mitigation plan.
- Supplier contracts for the primary network and cloud provider are signed; remote support is pending final confirmation but has a documented fallback.
Before we record the final go or no-go, does anyone see a blocker that we have not captured?

No additional blockers from my side.
If the remote support partner cannot confirm in time, we will adjust the SLA wording in A1 and A7 to reflect extended hours with a clear escalation path, as already agreed.
That should not require changes to pricing or bundle structure.

From operations and systems, I confirm there are no blockers.
The remaining invoice layout fixes are cosmetic and will be resolved before the first billing cycle.
We are ready to support the MVP bundles as defined.

No blockers from marketing and sales enablement.
Campaign assets are ready, and sales has been briefed on the bundles, pricing, and discount rules.
We will use the KPIs in A8 to track adoption and feedback from day one.

Nothing new to add.
I agree that with the current mitigations, we can proceed.
We just need to be disciplined in capturing early feedback so we can adjust quickly after launch.

Based on the checklist in A4, the plan in A6, and the mitigations in A5 and A8, I propose we proceed with launch as planned.
We will keep the remote support SLA adjustment as a fallback if the contract is not confirmed in time, but that does not block the launch.
I am recording this as a go decision, with the understanding that we will monitor closely in the first weeks.

I support the go decision.
From product and pricing, everything is in place and aligned with the constraints we set.
I will be available during the first week after launch to support any urgent questions from sales or customers.

Aligned with the go decision.
We will track the KPIs in A8, focusing on adoption, revenue, and early churn signals.
I will also set up a simple feedback form for sales and partners so we can feed insights into T12.

I confirm the go decision from operations.
We will keep a close eye on incident volumes and SLA performance in the first month and share data into the lessons learned work under T12.

On the post-launch follow-up, I suggest we:
- Use the KPI framework in A8 to run a 30-day and 90-day review.
- Collect structured feedback from sales, support, and a sample of customers.
- Prioritize improvement items into a backlog in line with T12.
I can help consolidate the feedback and draft the summary for stakeholders.

That plan works well.
I will schedule the 30-day and 90-day review checkpoints in A6 and reference A8 and T12 as the main inputs.
We will use this thread again after launch to share early results and lessons learned.
